extracted.intended_audience: researchers/investigators preparing grant applications to the CDMRP Tick-Borne Disease Research Program (TBDRP)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting research proposals to the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs Tick-Borne Disease Research Program (TBDRP), aligning projects with the program's mission, priorities, and review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision – Eliminate the health burden of tick-borne diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision – Eliminate the health burden of tick-borne diseases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level program goal: proposals should ultimately contribute toward reducing the overall health burden from tick-borne diseases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission – Fund innovative research to prevent, detect, and resolve tick-borne diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission – Fund innovative research to understand and provide solutions to prevent, detect, and resolve Lyme disease and other tick-borne diseases and conditions for the benefit of Service Members, Veterans, their Families and the American public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be framed as innovative, solution-oriented research that advances understanding or provides practical prevention, detection, or treatment approaches and benefits the stated populations (Service Members, Veterans, families, and the public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address fundamental gaps in pathogenesis and host response
rubrics_metrics.description: Much remains to be determined regarding tick-borne disease pathogenesis, including host-pathogen interactions and the human immune response to these pathogens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that investigate mechanisms of disease, host-pathogen biology, and the immune response are priorities; proposals should state how they fill specific knowledge gaps in pathogenesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention and control of tick exposure and natural disease cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need for better disease prevention in terms of controlling the natural cycle of disease and protecting people from tick bites by various means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research aimed at ecological control, interrupting transmission cycles, bite prevention technologies or strategies, and other means to reduce exposure are within program scope and should articulate expected impact on prevention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of direct detection/diagnostic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: For people who are bitten, having methods of direct detection of tick-borne pathogens is critical in guiding treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects developing or validating assays, point-of-care diagnostics, or other direct detection technologies that improve clinical guidance are encouraged and should demonstrate sensitivity, specificity, and clinical relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding and treating persistent symptoms
rubrics_metrics.description: More must be learned about the cause of persistent symptoms in Lyme disease and other tick-borne illnesses in order to establish the best treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that study causes, biomarkers, mechanisms, and evidence-based therapeutic approaches for persistent/post-infectious symptoms should articulate how outcomes will inform improved treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and impact (funding hallmarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TBDRP was established ... to support innovative and impactful research that addresses these fundamental issues and gaps in tick-borne diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are expected to demonstrate novelty and potential for meaningful impact on scientific understanding, public health, clinical care, or force readiness; state anticipated translational or practical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involvement of Lyme and tick-borne disease advocates in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Hallmarks of TBDRP funding include the involvement of Lyme and tick-borne disease advocates in our two-tier review process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program's review process includes consumer/advocate perspectives; applicants should be aware that consumer priorities may influence programmatic evaluation and may address potential stakeholder relevance in proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military relevance / threat to Service Members and dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: Hallmarks of TBDRP funding include ... the mission of addressing tick-borne diseases as a threat to military forces and their dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that explicitly address implications for military populations, operational readiness, or dependents (or clearly explain broader public health relevance) align with program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-tiered review process / programmatic and peer review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications undergo a structured review (peer review and programmatic review/panels). Applicants should consult program materials (peer review participants, programmatic panels) to understand evaluation stages and criteria used at each tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding research duplication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure proposals do not duplicate existing research; consult the program's resources and prior funded awards to justify novelty and avoid redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and consumer reviewer requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility Checklist; Program Consumer Reviewer Requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet program-specific eligibility rules and be aware of consumer reviewer roles/requirements; consult the linked Eligibility Checklist and Consumer Reviewer guidance for application eligibility and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available investigator resources and program guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources for Investigators; Funding Opportunity FAQ Document; How To Apply; Program Funding Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the provided resources (FAQ, How To Apply, Funding Opportunity pages, program summary sheet, strategic plan) to align proposals with program aims, follow application procedures, and address reviewer expectations.
